meta.title: Design Process — Movara Portfolio
meta.description: Requirements identification, solution generation, morph charts, and existing product comparison for the Movara transfer bench.

banner.heading: From Requirements to Concept
banner.lead: The behind-the-scenes analytical work that defined what the Movara transfer bench needed to be — and ruled out what it should not be.

requirements.heading: What Does the Ideal Solution Need to Do?
requirements.intro: Based on background research, clinical interviews, and market analysis, a structured set of functional, ergonomic, and safety requirements was established to guide the design process.

categories.title: Functional Requirements
items: Must enable lateral transfer across the full tub width
Must support longitudinal repositioning within the tub
Must provide adjustable seat height for varying users
Must allow rotational movement up to 180°
Add your functional requirements here — be as specific as possible

categories.title: Ergonomic Requirements
items: Seat surface must be comfortable for prolonged use in a wet environment
Controls must be operable with limited hand dexterity
Must accommodate users of varying weight and body dimension
Must not require the user to bear weight during transition

categories.title: Safety Requirements
items: Must not tip or shift under maximum design load
All moving parts must include mechanical travel limits
Materials must be corrosion-resistant and non-slip in wet conditions
Must meet or exceed applicable assistive device safety standards

categories.title: Usability & Accessibility
items: Must be installable without permanent bathroom modifications
Should be adjustable by the user or a single caregiver
Must be compatible with standard North American bathtub dimensions

morph_chart.heading: Comparing Design Attributes Side by Side
morph_chart.intro: A morph chart was used to systematically compare design alternatives for each functional attribute of the transfer bench. Each row represents a design parameter; each column represents an alternative implementation approach.
morph_chart.note: Edit the rows array below to reflect your actual morph chart data. Add or remove alternatives as needed.

comparison_matrix.heading: How Does Movara Compare to What Exists?
comparison_matrix.intro: An existing product comparison matrix was developed to evaluate commercially available transfer benches against the Movara design across key functional criteria. Products were scored on a 1–5 scale.
comparison_matrix.note: Edit the products array and criteria to match your actual comparison. Scores are out of 5.

decisions.title: Why a Rail-and-Carriage for Lateral Movement?
decisions.body: Replace this with your rationale. Consider: load-bearing capacity, corrosion resistance, simplicity of motion, friction characteristics in wet environments, and manufacturing feasibility. Reference your morph chart analysis.

decisions.title: Why Aluminium Alloy for the Frame?
decisions.body: Replace this with your material decision rationale. Consider: strength-to-weight ratio, corrosion resistance without coatings, machinability, cost, and recyclability. Reference your material selection matrix from the Testing page.

decisions.title: Why a 180° Rotation Limit?
decisions.body: Replace this with your rationale for the specific rotational limit. Consider: reach envelope required for typical bathing tasks, safety risk of unrestricted rotation, and stability of the frame at the limits of rotation.
